mission: Descent through the ring structure. Ring 4: seal boundary — Ben crosses it and his Force-sense drops away entirely. Ring 3: evacuation zone — doors standing open, vehicles pointed away. Ring 2: the city — homes, shops, a school, a child's toy on a step, vines reversing, flowers on shadow faces. Desh's grief-without-an-object lands without mysticism (PP25 pays). The ridgeline opens on the valley and the Scar is visible below. Per W2 Option α (CONDITIONAL FLEXIBILITY SLOT, NOT DEFAULT): a villain-refresh beat is preserved as capacity — Ben may, in the evacuation-zone passage, glimpse Veraine at distance on an opposing ridge, a figure standing still, watching the group descend, too far to pursue, gone before the binoculars focus. No exchange. No taunt. A sighting and a registration: she is already here, she has allowed herself to be seen, she did not stay. Default drafting assumption is that α is NOT executed — the slot remains a pacing-refresh pressure valve, and the chapter's villain-presence load continues via β (the ledger beat at s3). If α is executed at draft time, β collapses to a short coda in s3.
why_now: The Veranthos world-building pays off here. The ring structure is the book's most ambitious environmental design and it has to deliver in one chapter. The α slot lives in this scene because the evacuation-zone's open sight-lines and ridgeline geometry are the only place in the chapter where a distance-sighting is plausible; placing the capacity here preserves drafter latitude without restructuring later scenes.
conflict: The city is not a disaster zone. That is the horror. It is intact, overgrown, and wrong in the specific way a room is wrong when the furniture is right but the gravity is off. Desh's non-Force grief lands; Ben's Force-sense does not register his own hand reaching into a space that refuses to answer. If α is executed, Ben sees Veraine in the distance and does not pursue — the sighting is a frozen second in the middle of a descent that cannot pause for her.
turning_point: Ben stops walking at the ridgeline. The Scar is visible below — a three-meter vertical distortion of air where the Force was torn and never fully healed. Sight arrives before concept. If α is executed, the second turning-point is the moment Ben lowers the binoculars and finds the opposite ridge empty — a second kind of sight.
opening_hook: Ben steps through the seal boundary and the Force drops away — not thinned, not shifted. Gone.
closing_hook: Ahead, in the valley between ridgelines: the Scar. A roughly three-meter vertical line in the air where the Force was torn and never fully healed. Not glowing. Not pulsing. A visual distortion — wrong in the way that things are wrong when the eye can see them but the brain can't parse them. Ben stops walking
emotional_trajectory: Controlled descent -> escalating wrongness -> the devastating beauty of drift -> awe and horror at the Scar

stakes.personal: Ben experiencing the wound source — the thing the whole book has been leading to; Ben operating without Force-sense for the rest of the book
stakes.interpersonal: Each group member's reaction at different ring levels; Desh's non-Force grief lands as the book's claim about the Weave mattering to non-Force-users
stakes.external: Veraine is at the epicenter. Torin is orientating toward it. The stage is set.

setting: Veranthos surface — descending through rings: seal boundary, evacuation zone, city, approaching the valley
sensory_details: Ring 4 crossing: a hand reaching into space that refuses to register the hand; Ring 3: doors standing open, vehicles pointed away, a thousand years of overgrowth; Ring 2: the city — vines climbing and reversing, horizontal tree splits through walls, flowers blooming on shadow faces, no birds; Desh's grief-without-an-object settling in below the sternum without ever finding its object — a sadness about nothing that will not lift until leaving the zone; the Scar: heat shimmer without heat, barely visible straight on, unmistakable at an angle; CONDITIONAL (α-executed only): a distant figure on an opposing ridge, posture precise and unhurried, gone before the binoculars focus — the space where she stood continuing to be watched by Ben for a beat longer than is tactically reasonable
canon_elements_needed: Veranthos ring-structure world-building (seal boundary, evacuation zone, city, valley)
Force-wound phenomenology — full de-structuring vocabulary family (non-handrail variants)
action_beats: Ben steps through the seal boundary and stumbles as the Force drops away entirely
The group moves through the city's empty streets — buildings standing but wrong, vines reversing direction, flowers in shadow

CONDITIONAL (α slot, NOT default): in the evacuation-zone passage, Ben raises binoculars at movement on an opposing ridge, finds a figure watching them, loses her between two breath-cycles. No pursuit
Ben stops at the valley ridge and stares at the Scar — a three-meter vertical distortion where reality was torn and never healed
promises_paid: PP25 — the wound as lived galactic texture, not cosmic concept (Desh's grief lands in the evacuation-zone city)
notes: Use the full Veranthos world-building from extended_metadata.world_building extensively. The Scar is the reader's first direct look at the thing the book has been describing indirectly since Ch 1; it must feel like sight, not concept. Rotate Force-wrongness metaphor for Ben's seal-boundary crossing: a hand reaching into space that refuses to register the hand; do not reuse the 'ground dropping out' phrasing from Ch 13 nor the handrail family. Desh's non-Force grief must land without mysticism — force_mechanics.sensory_vocabulary.full_de_structuring.non_force_sensitive specifies the register: a sadness about nothing that will not lift until leaving the zone. Anti-pattern: the city is not rendered as disaster; the point is that it is intact and still wrong. Per W2 Option α, the conditional slot preserves capacity for a distance-sighting beat. Default drafting: α NOT executed. The slot is the chapter's pacing pressure-valve; use at draft time only if the chapter reads as needing a direct villain-refresh beat between Ch 16 and Ch 25. If α is executed: no chase; no attempted interception; no dialogue; the beat is a sighting, a frozen second, an absence where the figure was. Per W2 anti-pattern, Veraine's register if seen does not warm or sharpen because she is visible to Ben — she stands still, she is seen, she moves on. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate the phenomenology as theory. He sees, he cannot Force-sense, he stops walking. Voice: Zahn-procedural for the descent; one permitted Stover-dense beat for Ben's step through the seal boundary; one permitted Stover-dense beat for the Scar reveal. Primary anchor: Stover (the two permitted dense beats); supporting anchor: Zahn (procedural frame of the ring descent), Bujold (Ben's interior register at the Ring 4 crossing). Anti-patterns: (a) do not describe the ruined city as a disaster zone — intact and still wrong; (b) no combat; (c) if α is not executed, do not tease the slot or reference it in prose — the slot becomes invisible and β carries the villain-presence load at s3; (d) if α is executed, no interior narration of 'why did she want to be seen' — Ben registers the sighting and the descent continues.

conditional_slot.interaction: If alpha executed at draft time, beta collapses to a one-paragraph coda in s3. If alpha not executed, beta is the full ledger-entry beat.
